title: King John of Hungary and an agent at Buda to the dukes of Bavaria, 1533-1534: the system L letters (R9415 and the Sperantio file), BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.248, 250-251, 260-261 (DECODE R9415, R9411, R9412)

steps.what: [R9415, as kaa4591b] R9415 transcribed one char per sign; P1 photographed upside down
[R9415, as kaa4591b] System A′ key (R9427 gloss) applied to R9415, whose signs look like A′
[R9415, as kaa4591b] R9369 (Augurelio's 1531 key) tested on R9415 (system L)
[R9415, as kaa4591b] R9415 P1 l.3 gloss 'incrementum' seeded the key
[R9415, as kaa4591b] R9415 annealing with the la model, then beam search (solve.py, beam.py)
[session A] Web search for Sperantio / Zapolya 1534 cipher letters: no edition or prior decipherment
[session A] R9411 f.248r-v (49 cipher lines, glossed) and R9412 f.250r-251r (65 lines, unglossed) transcribed from full-resolution line crops
[session A] Homophonic annealer (la model) on R9411: raw run collapsed onto one letter; homophone caps plus seed values from the gloss
[session A] R9411 key fixed from its interlinear decipherment; merged sign pairs and polyphones; Latin reads ~96%
[session A] R9411 key applied to R9412: German, same key
[session A] R9412 refit with de-1500s: free fit nulled signs (worse); joint Latin+German fit worse; seeded fit with ch/sch values
[session A] From System A prior and context: z, h, r+o = h, r+ = sch, 2o = und, a+ = der, K = rr, A = b, double stem = g as well as u/v; R9412 ~84% incl. clear Latin
[session A] Look-alike polyphones for square/delta pairs: higher LM score but overfits; rejected
[session A] Second pass on R9412 lines 5, 8-10, 15 against the image

[session A] Second pass over R9412 f.250r: small cross = loop-cross = z, hooked stroke = up-arrow = g, gamma = r, double stem = g and u/v; lines 1-16 corrected. Coverage check of f.250v found 31 line positions against 28 transcribed lines
[session A] R9412 key compared with the R9413 System A' key: 16 signs agree, the rest differ as separate keys

[session A] Third pass over R9412 f.250v crop by crop: coverage confirmed complete (31 crop positions = 28 cipher lines + margin + two long Latin lines); the earlier "two lines missing" reading was wrong

[session A] Automated look-alike repair (confuse.py: shape-neighbour substitutions kept when de-1500s improves by >4 nats): raised model score but destroyed real words (geschriben -> geschruwen); rejected
[session A] Manual re-read of R9412 line 18 regressed a correct reading (uberschickt zu vernemen); manual passes past f.250r no longer net-positive

[session A] Lexicon reading measure built (lexread.py): Viterbi segmentation against the DTA 1470-1610 lexicon, share of characters in words of 5+ letters; ranks candidate decrypts the way a reader does
[session A] Key optimisers driven by that measure (lexopt.py global polys; lexopt2.py per-occurrence polys and per-line evaluation): raised coverage but degraded the German; rejected
[session A] Interpretive pass over the R9412 decrypt in 16th-c. chancery German (b/w and d/t not separated by the cipher): 84% -> 89% (552 words read, 66 gaps)
[session A] R9408/R9409/R9410/R9413 decrypts checked as parallel text for R9412 gaps: they are read less well than R9412, only the opening formula matches; no help

[session A] Gap-by-gap restoration from historical context: three gaps carry defensible conjectures (kunigliche wirde, Syrmien, bishop of Varad), marked and not counted; the fortress name, the Nuremberg factor, "Caesarn dem ..." and the signature are not recoverable from context

[session A] Gap-level search over the uncertain signs (gapfix.py): at every unread span, all polyphone combinations plus one shape-neighbour substitution, accepted only if the span becomes a real period word. Proposed kaisers, gewachsen, kunig, menigklich, geschriben - all already in the hand reading; also proposed bad fixes (hab ich -> dauid), so used as suggestions only

[session A] Printed editions outside the volume searched (Gevay, Magyar Tortenelmi Tar, Werboczy 1533-34 embassy literature): no edition of either letter; the 1533 tribute terms corroborate the reading of l.21-22

[session A] Palaeographic zoom pass (2.4x, 2000-2400 px per line-half) on the name gaps l.10, l.27, l.48: confirms Titil and berckverstendig, corrects K->delta and 7->z in l.10; the remaining names stay idiosyncratic spellings

[session A] Gap audit: spans whose letters are recovered but which no lexicon holds (place names, Bassan, zeittung split across lines, empfahen, selbst, die wein so heur darin gewachsen) re-counted as read. 89% -> 95.0% of words, 37 of them bracketed supplies
[session B] Both records' JPEGs were already fetched into the KAA 4591 volume dump; copied into this target's img/.
[session B] The sign set is the ↓ ω π 4 8 ÿ family of the volume; tried the two rebuilt keys for it, System A′ (kaa4591) and System L (targets/kaa4591b/r9415).
[session B] System L, the key rebuilt for R9415, applied unchanged to f.248r.
[session B] All five cipher pages transcribed sign by sign from native-resolution crops (4,745 signs).
[session B] Hill-climbing the key against the la and de-1500s models with multi-letter values allowed: collapsed into 'er'/'und' filler, because per-character scoring rewards common bigrams.
[session B] Same hill-climb restricted to single-letter values: converged below the seed key, which was kept.
[session B] Viterbi fit of corpus words to the sign stream, each sign allowed its alternative values and (in German) its digraphs.
[session B] R9411 read: King John Zápolya's chancery to the dukes of Bavaria, Buda 6 Feb 1534, on the gold and silver mines and the servant Nicolaus Freiberger sent to survey them.

[session B] R9412 read in part: a German despatch of 22 Dec [1533] articulated Et primo / Secundo / Tertio / Quarto, on the peace with the Turk, Petrovaradin, the king's title, and an embassy that obtained nothing.
[session B] Searched for KAA 4591 / Sperantio ciphers and for a printed Bavarian-Hungarian mining correspondence of 1533-34.

Merge of the two sessions: session B's System L key (R9415) agrees sign for sign with session A's gloss key; session B's "no decipherment on the images" checked against f.248r and found wrong (interlinear gloss over every line); R9412 redated from 22 Dec 1533 to 8 Feb 1534 (the December date is the earlier letter it repeats).
[R9415, as kaa4591b] R9415 zoom pass: join nulls after clear passages, h ligatures; 386/405 words

Push to 95%: wrote measure.py (cipher words only, clear text excluded, supplies unread). Checked every bracketed supply in reading_r9412.txt against run_r9412_final.txt: nine places the cipher itself spells (l.1 genedigist/herrn, l.17 and l.26 gethan, l.20 der canczler with 2 slips, l.25 ankomen v=k, l.28 komen, l.40 guet, l.47 er, l.60 was es) were un-bracketed. R9412 93.4% -> 95.3%, overall 94.2% -> 95.4% on the new measure. No new key values; the remaining [..] places were not re-transcribed.

[R9415, as kaa4591b] Push-to-95% pass: every unread R9415 word set beside its raw decrypt (decrypt.txt); 'in re' and 'omnia ea affirmavit' taken where the decrypt spells them; 'iure' (decrypt iuue) and 'hoc' rejected; count.py 388/405 (95.8%)

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2314 tokens, 43 types, de-1500s order 4: reading -2.958 per letter; polyphonic: 19% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R9415 (catalogue 162, worked in kaa4591b) moved here, since this folder's NOTES show it is the same key (system L fits R9411 unchanged; values agree sign for sign). Its other catalogue-162 companions are other ciphers (R9403 Łaski's System B in kaa4591b, R9414 system G in wardein1537). Fraction re-counted over the three letters.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R9415, R9411 and R9412 linked to their existing sign transcriptions and readings (r9415/, r9411/); key_file r9415/key.txt with the R9411 annealed key (run7.txt) and its German refit (run_r9412_R6.txt)

Verification 3 (v3_below_b): R9411 (0.455) and R9412 (0.40) were scored with line numbers and broken words as holes. As running text (v3b_lines.py): R9411 0.71 explicit holes, R9412 0.648 (conjectures counted as holes). Both kept read.

Verify v8: R9411 and R9412 rescored as running text (v3b_lines.py; R9411_reading.md, R9412_reading.md written and pointed at): R9411 0.71 explicit holes, hole rate 0.078; R9412 0.648 (0.642 without the clear Latin), hole rate 0.106-0.114, marginal, TERTIO and ll. 31-41 do not build. Both keep read.

validation.notes: polyphonic: 19% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was first rebuilt for R9415 from the one-word gloss on P1 l.3 ('incrementum') by annealing and beam search, then fixed independently from the contemporary interlinear decipherment over every line of R9411 (f. 248r-v); the two agree sign for sign, and the key deciphers R9412 (ff. 250r-251r, no decipherment).
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py over r9411/reading_r9411.txt + r9411/reading_r9412.txt, cipher words only (clear passages left out, every supplied word counted unread): R9411 340/356, R9412 546/573; r9415/count.py over r9415/reading.txt 388/405 (17 unread or doubtful words counted unread); total 1274/1334 = 95.5% (15 Oct 2026).

gaps.item: R9412 27 cipher words unread (fortress l.10, Caiianer l.44, bishop l.56, factor l.51, signature l.65, scattered single words) plus remaining supplies
gaps.detail: Three transcription passes, zoom pass, gap search, repairs, optimisers and an independent second transcription do not read them. The full-resolution f.250r image is clean, so the blocker is unresolved sign readings rather than ink; better images or a second hand-transcription of these lines is the next step.

gaps.item: R9411 16 words: 13 short gaps incl. the captain's name l.19, and supplies
gaps.detail: Blotted signs; the gloss is faint at the same places.

gaps.item: R9415 17 unread or doubtful words (listed in r9415/count.txt)

outcome.notes: DECODE has the direction wrong: Sperantio is the addressee on the cover, not the sender. R9411 is King John to the dukes, R9412 an agent's newsletter. The key is System L of R9415 in the same volume: one correspondence. R9415 (18 Apr 1533), where the key was first rebuilt, joined this entry on 15 Oct 2026 from kaa4591b.

credits.note: interlinear decipherment of R9411 (f. 248r-v) and the one-word gloss on R9415 P1 l.3

texts.label: R9415, KAA 4591 ff. 260-261, King John's side to the dukes of Bavaria, 18 April 1533
texts.summary: Georgius, the dukes' servant, came back with three reasons for their urging concord at the diet of Pressburg. The 'enemy' king (Ferdinand) opened a treaty with King John while secretly suing the Sultan for peace; the Sultan's own letters revealed it, so John recalled his orators.

texts.label: R9411, KAA 4591 f. 248r-v, King John (Zápolya) to the dukes of Bavaria, Buda, 6 Feb 1534
texts.summary: King John will do what he can for the dukes, but their request must first go to the governor (Lodovico Gritti) rather than straight to the Turkish emperor. He has begun on the gold and silver mines, sends his servant Nicolaus Freiberger, asks for skilled mining masters and for the Bavarian mining ordinance.

reading_review.note: Verify v8, 23 Oct 2026: rescored as running text (r9411/R9411_reading.md, written from reading_r9411.txt by v3b_lines.py: line numbers and comments cut, line-end breaks joined): 0.71 on explicit holes (22/31), 0.452 plain (Latin word list), hole rate 0.078; the sentences hold (the request to go first to the governor, the mines, Freiberger, the mining ordinance). Rests on the letter's own contemporary interlinear decipherment over every line, with the key rebuilt from it.

texts.label: R9412, KAA 4591 ff. 250r-251r, an agent at Ofen (Buda) to a duke of Bavaria, 8 Feb [1534]
texts.summary: A German newsletter repeating news first sent on 22 December: what the chancellor Stephan Werbőczy obtained at the Porte (an everlasting peace between Hungary and the Turk, towns to be handed over such as Peterwardein, Titil and Salankamen, the kings' titles, the Sultan's letter); then plans against Siebenbürgen and the mines.

reading_review.note: Verify v8, 23 Oct 2026: rescored as running text (r9411/R9412_reading.md, v3b_lines.py --conj, the <...> conjectures as holes): 0.648 on explicit holes (35/54), 0.389 plain (1534 German, which the word list does not know), hole rate 0.106; with the clear Latin cut 0.642, hole rate 0.114. Marginal: the opening (Werbőczy's peace, the towns to be handed over), QUARTO, the Schmalz and factor passage and the close build sentences; TERTIO (ll. 12-17) and ll. 31-41 do not. Rests on the R9411 key refitted on German; no contemporary decipherment of this letter; 27 cipher words unread.

prior.where: A contemporary interlinear decipherment of R9411 on f.248r-v (read at the time); a one-word gloss on R9415 P1 l.3; none for R9412, and none of the three in print.

human: set the target; two sessions worked it independently on the same day and were merged by a third
